newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt hit by profit-taking, weak U.S. bonds.
newsitem.headline: German debt hit by profit-taking, weak U.S. bonds.

text.p: German Bund futures were hit by profit-taking and a weaker Treasury market on Monday after posting sharp gains late last week.
Traders said they remain bullish on the contract, but that with German economic data due on Wednesday, they were reluctant to add to what has been a 140 basis point gain over the last two weeks.
At 1458 GMT, the December DTB Bund future was down 22 basis points, pushed down from more moderate losses late in the afternoon by weaker U.S. debt.
Traders said that although Bunds suffered a correction on Monday, they believe that Germany's slow economic growth should create a bond-friendly environment for the near-term.

The first test of that theory could come on Wednesday when third quarter GDP is released. Economists surveyed by Reuters on Monday said they expect GDP figures will show an annual increase of around two-percent -- up from the second quarter's 1.2 percent growth, but still slow. Traders said such a figure would likely be neutral for German debt while a view held among some economists that GDP would grow less than two-percent should boost Bunds to yet new highs.
As is usual, however, U.S. debt markets will be the key to any further gains with signs of a stronger U.S. economy hurting Treasuries and global debt markets.

Bunds should outperform any weakness in the U.S. market, however. After the release of the November NAPM index which hurt Treasuries on Monday, Bunds gained two basis points against their U.S. counterparts and the spread stood at 53 basis points.

Chartists said they see support for the Decmeber contract at 102.28 and resistance at 102.55. A breach of that resistance point would see the contract targeting 102.70, they said. --Frankfurt Newsroom + 49 69 756525
